title: A weekend in London and the Exposition year
summary: He visited London briefly to hear Ambrose's band, and they sort out whether the Paris Exposition was 1937 or later.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But in London, I... I wasn't in London, I remember.
Did you go to London to...?
Yeah. But I never stayed too long. I knew a guy(?), Ambrose.
Did you go with Bobby Martin there?
No, I went on my own. I went on a jaunt.
Was that at a time when Bobby Martin was off?
Yeah, when Bobby Martin was there.
Well, how long were you over there?
Well, it was just for a weekend or something.
I see, you just looked it over.

Yeah, in a sense. I wanted to see Ambrose's band. Really we went up over there, because they used to say... I mean, when they were in Paris they used to say their band didn't play like this... They were playing an engagement with Raymond Tour(?)... It was a good band.
Oh, yes.
For that time, you know. You must remember that that was the year of the French Exposition, the year
Ramirez - 62
(?) came over.
Now, which year was the Exposition? Because I went...
Well, what the hell were they having... I went to New York in '37. But I went to Paris when they were having the Exposition. Did that not run two years?
Maybe.
It seems to me that I couldn't have gone to New York and to Paris the same year. I wouldn't have had money enough.
New York had one at the same time, didn't they? [1939]

Yeah, but I came here in '37. And I know one year when I was in Paris before the War, there was a big exposition, because we went, and each province had a wine lodge, and we drank ourselves all around here, you know, like for a nickel of this fine wine at each one. I thought that was '38. But maybe. Maybe they had...
Maybe it stayed around.
Well, '39 I was there, I know. Because that was before the war.
